properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: VERNARD L SHUMAKER
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/14/2024
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 8179627
Permit API: 129-27948
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/14/2024
Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. The well name and API was scratched into a pipe clamp, this does not meet the posting requirements of 3211(G). The line leading to the production tank appears to have failed and separated. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks. Gas was leaking from the base of the wellhead as seen in the attached photographs at 12%LEL. The line leading into the production tank appears to have separated and was leaking gas at 79%Gas. The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department. 78.88(d) - Failure to notify the Department and take corrective action to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion or other signs of deterioration that compromises the integrity of the well. 78.73(a) - Failure to operate the well in accordance with 25 PA code Chapter 78 and ensure the integrity of the well is maintained. 78.74 - Venting of gas to the atmosphere that produces a hazard to public health and safety.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/23/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 996037
Permit API: 015-23794
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 5/23/2023
Comments: On 5/23/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Deremer well site. It was 58 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, one of the workers radioed the Chesapeake company man of my site visit. I did not immediately see him and started my inspection. Later, I did meet the company man, Trey Villarreal as I was conducting the site inspection. Trey described current operations as follows: Precision drilling rig 560 is on site drilling four new wells to completion. Three existing wells are being kept in production during the drilling process. The rig was currently drilling the Deremer 126HC and was at 20,349 feet with TD being 23,700 feet. This is their third well with one left to drill. Cement silos and water tanks containing municipal water are staged outside of secondary containment on the west side of the rig. I did not witness any cement trucks unloading during the inspection.The drilling rig and ancillary equipment was stationed on plastic lined secondary containment that is protected by drilling mats. The three existing well heads have been protected from damage by cages. Oil based mud tanks, diesel based mud tanks and freshwater tanks were stationed in secondary containment along the south side of the rig. A 60' x 15' x 1" water puddle next to the oil based mud tanks and production equipment field tested at 2.83 mS conductance. A 20' x 20' water and mud puddle area near the south side of the production fluid tanks and east of the oil based and diesel based mud tanks field tested at 3.46 mS conductance. This water puddle connects to the 60' x 15' water puddle in picture seven. I collected sample number 9551050 from this location for laboratory analysis. Trey did say that he would have the water puddle vacuumed up. I also witnessed a 2' x 1' water puddle outside of secondary containment along the south side of the pad that field tested at 5.16 mS conductance.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover with steeper sections of the fill slope stabilized with rock. PCSM is addressed on site by four retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the areas where the elevated conductance fluid was discovered and clean/report as necessary.2. Use good chemical handling procedures when storing and using chemicals to prevent causing pollution to the waters of the commonwealth.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/13/2022
Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Violation ID: 8187541
Permit API: 003-22657
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Fawn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/13/2024
Comments: On May 13, 2024 the Department conducted an incident inspection in regards to a spill that occurred at the Sun Mine Well Site (ESCGP-3 issued on 9/11/2023 and expires on 9/10/2028) on May 10, 2024. According to Derek Zofchak of Range Resources, the spill occurred at 12 PM when drill cuttings and soap slurry fluid entered the flare stack eco tank (which normally separates fluids from gas), the float on the pump within the eco tank malfunctioned and as a result, fluid (approximately 30 gallons of drill cuttings and soap slurry) that normally would not get carried over to the flare stack ended up spewing out of the flare stack as a fine mist onto the graveled well pad and well pad fill slope. At the time of the inspection, Range Resources notified the Department that the spill had been remediated. Two roll off dumpsters were on site filled with waste material, the well pad appeared to be scraped on the left hand side of the flare stack, and new seed and mulch was seen on the the fill slope and berm directly in front of and to the left-hand side of the flare stack. Soil conductivity readings were taken to determine if any areas were still contaminated, a background was done on the far back side of the well site perimeter upslope (0.03 mS) then readings were taken outside of the approximate release area to the far left of the flare stack on the pad (0.0085 mS and 0.016 mS), then moving forward into the approximate release area (0.0146 mS), another was taken fairly close to the flare stack on the left-hand side in a wet looking spot in the gravel (0.327 mS), directly next to the flare stack in a wet-looking section of gravel (0.293 mS). Then a reading was taken from the right side of the flare stack where Range claims was not impacted and therefore was not scrapped (0.088 mS). A reading was taken directly behind the flare stack right at the base of the berm before the fill slope (0.138 mS), in the berm directly behind the flare stack (0.081 mS), outside of the area that Range replaced on the fill slope where they say was not impacted (0.130 mS), and lastly three were taken from the area of the fill slope that was replaced (0.100 mS, 0.131 mS and 0.209 mS). Based on the soil conductivity readings, it appears that all contaminated material that was present on the fill slope, berm and the well pad to the left/in front of the flare stack has been removed. Range stated that the flare stack eco pump was taken apart for examination and nothing was found to be wrong with it. According to Range this was just a random malfunction and they do not anticipate that it will occur again. The Department recommends Range place the flare stack inside secondary containment in case this were to occur again.Based on todays inspection the Department concludes this release has been immediately corrected in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).

Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both pads. DEP Environmental Trainee John Rogers and DEP Geoscientist Sam Louderback accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on Pad B. On Pad B, the sump remains installed where fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) was observed on the pad surface. Fluid is present within the sump approximately two feet below the pad surface. The EC of this fluid is 2.19 mS/cm. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed on or off the pad. In the rock-lined ditch along the northwest edge of the pad, two small puddles of fluid were found which had a petroleum odor and a sheen. I notified the company man of the presence of these puddles before leaving the location. On Pad A, we met with company man Grant Boyd upon arriving on location. He told us that excavation had been done after the previous inspection on the pad near the northeast corner of the well site secondary containment. Multiple puddles were observed in this area during this inspection which had an EC between 3.43 mS/cm and 4.33 mS/cm. An additional puddle was observed along the pad edge within the brush barrier along the side of the pad. This puddle had an EC of 2.09 mS/cm. I took a sample, sample #0718-178, from this puddle and sent it to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Li, Br, and Al. I notified the company man of my findings before leaving the location. In a phone call with Rick Hall on the same day at 13:29, I relayed my observations on both pads to Mr. Hall. He said that he would have the puddles investigated and remediated. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad B.

Comments: On 3/31/2026, Next Level Energy notified the Department that the Palermo 1 OG well (039-24118) sprayed an indeterminant amount of liquid mist out onto approximately of an acre while actively plugging the well. The Department dispatched Emergency Response to the site to evaluate.An onsite inspection in response to the complaint was conducted on 4/01/2026 by Elyse Henshaw, Water Quality Specialist, and Kyle Thomas, Oil and Gas Inspector. Upon arrival, Henshaw and Thomas found the impacted soil scraped up and piled around the well head. The soil was covered with tarps to prevent rainwater from carrying it from the site. Henshaw and Thomas conferred with representatives from Next Level Energy and Diversified to learn that the soil would be removed by the end of the week and plugging operations would resume. Henshaw and Thomas walked into the wooded area adjacent to the well site to find a waxy film on the leaf litter. Thomas believed the film was from the gel, a biodegradable material, used to put down hole to kill the well rather than residual crude oil. Henshaw and a representative from Diversified walked into the wooded area to determine the extent of the spray and did not find a sheen on top of the puddles within the area. Additionally, they utilized conductivity probes to determine no brine water was sprayed into the woods. They also tested multiple points in the area that had been scraped up to determine all contaminated soils had been removed. A small amount of brine water remained around the well head and will be removed when plugging operations conclude. Fresh topsoil, seed and mulch will be brought in to stabilize and restore the impacted area. On 04/07/2026 a copy of this report was sent to Diversified Production LLC at painspections@dgoc.com for their review.

Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a complaint at the Whiteko 4 well site in Luzerne Township, Fayette County.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 3 and 4). The operator's information is posted on the meter box (see photo 7). Staining was observed on the ground underneath the meter box (see photos 8 and 13). However, this staining may be caused by algae growth due to no elevated conductivity and a moss-like odor exhibited in this location (see photo 8). No petroleum odor or residue was observed in this stained area. Some rust was observed on brine tank, however it appears to be sound at the time of inspection. Standing rainwater was observed in the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank. The conductivity level of this standing water underneath the brine tank valve was not indicative of a brine fluid leak (see photo 12 and 13). The well site appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1 and 5). Tire rutting that varies in severity was observed in the access road and low-hanging vegetative overgrowth was observed that appears to be capable of hindering vehicular access to the well site in the event of an emergency (see photos 14-16 and 19). The tire rutting was most severe near the entrance of the access road that also made vehicular access to the site difficult. What appears to be a steep third-party road was observed that intersects with the access road. A deep erosion rill was observed going downslope perpendicular to the access road that appears to be capable hindering vehicular access to the well site in the event of an emergency and resulting in accelerated erosion and sedimentation (see photos 17 and 18).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the operator clear the low-hanging vegetative overgrowth along the access road to ensure a clearance height that continues to permit vehicular access to site.Violations shall be issued against the tire rutting and deep erosion rill in the access road, as it appears that it may hinder vehicular access to the well site and result in accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite.

Comments: On 10/31/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 43 degrees, overcast and lightly sprinkling when I arrived on location. Rainfall has impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. The pad has not been reclaimed and the temporary access road and temporary bridges remain installed.When I arrive on the active site, I met Seneca's Wes Sammins who described current operations as follows: Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up over the 70HU, and had started drilling surface on 10/28/2025. The rig was currently drilling the intermediate at 1568 feet with the intermediate going to 3350 feet, then to total depth at 23514 feet. Wes expects to drill one more well that is in the process of being repermitted. Six wells have been completed this run. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. 12 frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment around the drilling rig. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Sand separators were attached to the wells, the sand separators all connected to two frac tanks. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Liquid in a 5' x 40' puddle on the unprotected ground north of the GPUs field tested at 1875 mS conductance. I discussed this with Wes who arranged for the liquid to be removed.A 40 foot channel of water immediately east of the central outfall from the pad field tested at 2030 uS conductance. Liquid draining from the north center outfall into the basin field tested at 2020 uS conductance. Liquid in the sediment basin next to the northeast overflow field tested at 1380 uS conductance. Liquid was observed flowing through the northern most compost filter sock and leaving the site; the liquid field tested at 1201 uS conductance. Liquid flowing past the LOD field tested at 1409 uS conductance.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 6/26/2023 at 0855 hours. The weather was 73 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remains at the access road entrance.Areas excavated related to the produced water release from 4/6/2023 remain exposed at this time. Constructed sumps remain in place to collect additional stormwater. Water that has collected within the excavated areas was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) and ranged from 970us/cm to 2.15mS/cm today. The DEP recommends continuing to collect water from these areas and disposing of it properly. The stormwater control basin impacted by the 4/6/2023 release was observed to be retaining water today (photo #4). Water within the basin was field measured for EC at ~430us/cm. The stormwater channel that diverts water to the basin remains excavated. All impacted material collected from the 4/6/2023 release appears to have been removed from the site. Pipeline construction has opened up two of the topsoil stockpiles onsite. The topsoil stockpiles have been temporarily stabilized with straw. A small erosion channel was observed on the northern cut slope of the pad (photo #3). The DEP recommends repairing the erosion channel to prevent further damage to the slope. All secondary containment structures remain intact and no leaks or other issues were noted today. No new evidence of spills/releases was observed. Violations cited against API #015-23733 on 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1000 hours.

Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Lutz 015" Marcellus well site.Mike Mcnett (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday February 8, 2023 to report an estimated 10 gallon release of produced liquid from the dumpline onto the pad surface. I spoke with McNett on site. Two days ago Well Services was trying to unload one of the Marcellus wells at this site. When they sent produced liquid from the GPU, a union on the dumpline broke. They immediately stopped the flow, but an estimated 10 gallons leaked onto the pad surface. Immediately after the release, workers removed four 5 gallon buckets full of mostly gravel pad material under the pipe that leaked. Today they are inspecting all the unions on the dumpline. A crew is removing the insulation from the pipe during this inspection. I got electrical conductivity (EC) readings 0.80-1.4 mS/cm from moist soil below the leak. McNett filled a 55 gallon drum with additional impacted pad material during this inspection. EC readings in the pad material after that were 0.21-0.44 mS/cm. Pad material outside of the spill area has EC of 0.10-0.33.Violations cited to the 015-20372 permit are considered immediately corrected.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.08-0.57 mS/cm with an Oakton PCST 5. Air temp 42FJLP

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an incident response inspection that was conducted on-site.Kris Bowser with AMS Energy contacted me on Thursday, July 14, 2022, to report a brine spill that had occurred on AMS's Barrett Pattison 5 Well Site. The spill had been discovered earlier the same day. A valve had been broken off of a fiberglass brine tank that was used on-site. Kris believed that the valve had likely been damaged by an ATV that had gotten too close to the tank. Fluid from the tank had recently been hauled out. Kris estimated that less than a barrel of brine had been spilled onto the ground near the tank.Kris met me on-site to view the spill. The damaged valve had been repaired. Most of the spilled brine appeared to have settled in a swale that ran next to the tank. The impacted area was clearly marked with dead vegetation. My soil conductivity probe was used to verify the extent of the impacted area. Elevated readings were not observed beyond the area marked by the dead vegetation. A plan for addressing the impacted soil was discussed with Kris. The soil should be excavated and hauled to a landfill. Kris indicated the AMS would provide the Department with a receipt of disposal from the landfill once the soil has been disposed of.

Comments: This follow up inspection was conducted to evaluate the open violations at this site which were issued on November 21, 2023. The access road and site location have not been stoned. The culverts, ditches, and sumps at this location have been installed. The areas of earth disturbance along the banks of the site and access road have been mulched, however, several areas are not sufficient due to washing away over time. These areas will require added temporary stabilization. Upon arriving at the site at approximately 13:15, there was no precipitation occurring. At approximately 13:30, it began to lightly rain. It was noted that the access roads leading to the proposed wells upslope of the Hastings SDT 47 proposed well site showed evidence of accelerated erosion (see Photos 1 and 2). Due to the up slope road surface not having stone, that the up slope ditches, culverts, and sumps became overwhelmed with sediment laden water (see Photo 3). The culvert at the Hastings SDT 47 site location was receiving a large volume of sediment laden water from the up slope roads (see Photo 4). This sediment laden water was traveling through the woods and directly discharging into Hastings Run (see Photos 5 and 6). Down stream of the discharge, the sediment laden water is clearly pictured from bank to bank (see Photo 7). This photo was taken after the rain had stopped at approximately 14:00. The rain was varying in intensity over the course of the 30 minutes with approximately 10 minutes of heavy down fall. A voicemail was left with the operator, Steven Tachoir, to discuss the results from this inspection. It was recommend to stone the access roads and site location as quickly as possible as weather permits. The issued violations noted from November 21, 2023 will be noted as outstanding as a result of this inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-11-13 to Penneco Oil Co Inc in Somerset Twp, Washington county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Penneco Oil Co Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-11-13
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 868037
Permit API: 125-22807
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-11-13
Comments: On 11/13/19 a follow up inspection of the site was conducted in response to violations noted on 7/14/16 and in preparation for a meeting with the operator. The following was observed: >>The initial inspection on 7/14/16 found: "A large erosion channel leading off of the access road and into the surrounding brush was found near coordinates N40°11'03.29” W80°01'01.32”. This constitutes violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion." >>An inspection on 8/15/19 found: "The erosion channel described in the prior inspection was remediated and in good condition. A second channel extended along the middle half of the access road on the uphill side. This constitutes violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion." >>At the time of inspection barren and possibly eroded soils were found near around the outlet of the under road culvert at the location of the initial erosion channel near the bottom of the access road. Additional erosion channels were noted forming along much of the improved access road with some extending away from the access road into the surrounding brush. These continue to constitute violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, 25 Pa. Code § 102.4(b)(1), and 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)(1) for failure to design and implement measures to prevent accelerated erosion. Increased monitoring and remediation possibly including rock check dams are encouraged. A meeting is scheduled for 11/14/19 with the operator to discuss ongoing conditions and remediations options at this and other nearby sites.
